messages:
alice.dev: Customer reporting sudden 429 spikes and intermittent 401s during repeated regenerations. Pattern shows it happens when they mix 32k + 64k variants in the same session and do parallel regen attempts. Example X-Request-Id: req_0a1b2c3d. Any immediate guidance?

ben.support: Thanks — can you paste a minimal repro (curl + headers) and a few failing request ids? 401s usually indicate auth hiccups but combined with 429s suggests per-model RPM/TPM or concurrency exhaustion. Are they fanouting to multiple variants?

alice.dev: Minimal repro below — they hit two variants at once and do a small prefetch then 3x regen. Sometimes the 2nd regen returns 401. Curl (sanitized):

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-64k-alpha","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<~60k tokens>"}],"max_tokens":1024}'
```

They also issue the same to `rwd-32k-beta` at the same time.

carla.prod: Looking at logs in our support sandbox: requests from the same API key are hitting the per-model RPM cap on rwd-64k-alpha. Long contexts eat a lot of token budget so TPM is exhausted sooner. Regens that fanout concurrently keep KV/cache activity high which can amplify token throughput > per-model limits and cause 429s. The 401s in these cases are transient failures in the auth path to the dedicated pool during high burst (we see a few token-exchange timeouts). Quick mitigations:
- Reduce concurrent regen threads (limit client fanout).
- Pin to one variant where possible (avoid simultaneous 32k+64k fanout).
- Add exponential backoff with jitter on 429/401.
- Pre-warm with small prefix calls to warm KV cache instead of full long-context prefetch.

ben.support: Also confirm account-level quota (some customers hit an account RPM even if per-model still has headroom). Please gather the last 5 req ids and trace links.

alice.dev: Sample req ids: req_0a1b2c3d, req_0a1b2c3e, req_0a1b2c3f. Trace link for one: https://console.redwood/trace/0a1b2c3d (customer redacted).

doug.oncall: I'm pulling runtime traces now. Early signal: throttles triggered by token-rate (TPM) for rwd-64k-alpha. We also observed auth token exchange failures to the dedicated pool under burst which produced 401s; those were transient. I'm opening an eng-runtime ticket to dig into auth retry backpressure and rate-limiter behavior when long-context requests spike. Immediate operational advice: route heavy-prefetch to 32k variant or serialize regens, and implement Retry-After handling.

ingest-bot: incident-note: escalated to eng-runtime as IR-2026-78, attached traces and example payloads.

carla.prod: To be explicit (examples from our internal logs): rwd-64k-alpha approx config observed: RPM=40, TPM=1200, max_concurrency=8. If the client does 10 simultaneous regen calls (fanout across variants) they will hit 429s quickly. Also note: a 60k-context request counts ~60k tokens against TPM even before completion for some accounting windows — so a few large requests will burn TPM fast.

alice.dev: Shared workaround with the customer: reduce concurrent regen to 4, prefer a single model variant, add 200-500ms jittered backoff on 429/401, and fall back to 32k variant if 64k fails. Customer tried and saw immediate reduction in 429/401 occurrences. Leaving ticket open for eng-runtime to root cause the auth-timeout under burst.

ben.support: Good first response. Please attach full traces + headers (Authorization masked) to the eng-runtime ticket and ask for guidance on whether they should purchase Reserved/Dedicated capacity or we should increase per-model caps for their account. Follow up with billing if needed.

carla.prod: Adding checklist for eng-runtime: include the X-Request-Ids above, the payload sizes, whether prefetch was used, and the account id. Recommend we also review rate-limit headers behavior (we should ensure Retry-After is present and accurate for model-level throttles).

alice.dev: Done — ticket updated with traces and the customer's acceptance of the workaround. Will monitor and update once eng-runtime replies. Thanks all.
